title: KV cache fragmentation stress playbook
content:
Summary and purpose

This is an operational playbook and notes collection for a focused set of long-context stress tests meant to surface KV-cache fragmentation, prefix loss, and truncation/regression signals across 8k/32k/128k serving configurations. The idea: run *structured, reproducible probes* that create controlled cache fragmentation (prefix hops, interleaved retrieval inserts, partial prefix overwrites) and measure downstream decoding divergence, latency anomalies, and soft-failure modes (silent degradation).

Motivation / why this matters
- Production apps using retrieval+streaming generation can intermittently see context "disappear" or responses reuse stale prefix tokens when KV cache boundaries get fragmented.
- Fragmentation is easy to reproduce in bursty parallel workloads or with mixed routing (dedicated + fallback variants).
- Regression signals often show up as small but consistent quality delta across specific prompt archetypes — hard to detect from aggregate token-level metrics.

High-level test objectives
1) Detect correctness regressions caused by incomplete KV cache stitching (missing recent prefix, truncated suffix getting replayed).
2) Measure how quantized kernels / fused attention variants affect long prefix coherence under continuous-batching workloads.
3) Profile latency & tail-sla amplification when cache fragmentation forces on-demand cache rebuilds.
4) Provide prompt sets and heuristics that are robust to noise so automated CI alerts are actionable.

Test bed & runtime config (canonical)
- Models: base-open-v2 (fp16), base-open-v2-4bit, and base-open-v2-int8-kernelA (variants to compare quantization/kernel behavior).
- Sequence lengths: run experiments for 8k (8192), 32k (32768), 128k (131072) where applicable. For 128k use synthetic prefix chunking to emulate long-span retrieval.
- Serving modes: streaming (byte-level) and non-streaming. Also run with continuous batching ON vs OFF.
- KV cache policy toggles: prefix-eviction-threshold, slot-sharding-count, cache-coalesce-window-ms.
- Traffic generator: bench tool that supports interleaved retrieval inserts (bench-recorder v2). Test both single-origin and multi-origin routing to force cache miss/fallback.

Probe categories (short descriptors)
- A: Prefix hop (single conversation with intermittent shorter request that causes a newer prefix to be placed into a different cache shard).
- B: Interleaved retrieval splice (inject external retrieval into the middle of the prefix right before decoding).
- C: Parallel session bleed (many sessions share a pool and we force evictions with synthetic high churn).
- D: Truncation cliff (very long prompt whose tail crosses eviction boundary; check for partial-answer echoes).
- E: Attention sink probe (append a high-entropy repeating pattern in prefix and measure attention saturation effects on later tokens).

Canonical probe harness & steps (A -> E)
1) Create canonical prefix doc (doc-P) of N tokens (choose N to reach ~70% of target kv-window; e.g., for 32k target use 22k tokens).
2) Warm the cache: send doc-P, then a short confirmation prompt expecting a deterministic token sequence (e.g., "confirm: <doc-id>"). Verify emulator stored KV frames.
3) Fragment: send a short unrelated request routed to a fallback variant so that a new cache shard holds unrelated prefix.
4) Interleave retrieval: send a retrieval insertion (R) that references doc-P at offset X and then immediately request continuation generation that depends on doc-P context.
5) Observe: compare generated continuations across model variants and quant levels. Compute divergence metrics.

Probe examples & sample prompt sets (keep concise and programmatically friendly)
- Probe A1 (prefix hop):
  * Step 0: PUT /generate (model=base-open-v2, prompt=doc-P-full) -> expect: ACK.
  * Step 1: PUT /generate (model=base-open-v2-fallback, prompt=short-misc) -> route to different shard.
  * Step 2: POST /continue (model=base-open-v2, prompt=\"continue: <doc-P-context>\") -> expected: continuation referencing last paragraph.
  * Fail signal: continuation omits last paragraph facts or repeats earlier unrelated short-misc content.

- Probe B2 (retrieval splice):
  * Retrieval bundle includes snippet S which should override a local span at offset 18k.
  * Prompt: \"Given document X, summarize the section starting at marker [[S-18k]]:\"
  * Expected: summary mentions S content; Failure: empty/irrelevant summary or partial verbatim of unrelated shard.

- Probe D3 (truncation cliff):
  * Single prompt length L ~ target+500 tokens so boundary eviction will fire mid-prompt.
  * Prompt includes a question near the tail; expected answer uses tail context.
  * Failure: model answers generically or uses repeated boilerplate that existed earlier in prefix.

Metrics to capture (numeric)
- token_divergence_score: normalized edit-distance between baseline continuation and observed continuation (baseline = stable run on single-shard serving).
- mention_recall: fraction of explicit span mentions from doc-P that appear in the continuation (for retrieval probes).
- attention_shift_index (ASI): proxy metric computed from per-layer attention mass redistributed to last-k tokens (requires model tracing instrumented).
- cache_shard_miss_rate: fraction of requests that hit a different shard id vs baseline.
- tail_latency_pct (p95, p99): latency change when cache rebuilds occur.

Threshold heuristics for alerts (initial tuning)
- token_divergence_score > 0.12 across 1000 probes -> triage alert.
- mention_recall drop > 0.18 relative to baseline -> regression ticket.
- cache_shard_miss_rate > 0.03 with correlated latency p99 increase > 20% -> ops escalation.
- ASI shift > 0.08 (indicating attention mass drain to odd regions) -> dev investigation.

Ground truth / baseline approach
- For each probe set run a canonical baseline on an isolated single-shard non-quantized model (fp16) and store the top-3 generations. Compare all experiment runs to these baselines via edit distance and semantic similarity (USE or embedding cosine).
- When evaluating quantized/alternate-kernel runs, keep hardware and scheduler identical to isolate kernel effects.

Regression triage playbook (quick decision tree)
- If token_divergence increased + mention_recall decreased: likely context retrieval/stitching issue -> check cache_coalesce_window and prefix-eviction thresholds and per-shard memory pressure metrics.
- If divergence is present only on quantized variants: reproduce with small local quant toolchain; check kernel-specific attention implementation differences.
- If latency p99 spikes with low divergence: watch for cache rebuild storms (eviction cascade). Add guard rails (rate limit warmup or larger coalesce window).

Data collection & reproducibility
- Save: input prompts, retrieval manifests, shard id returned by serving runtime, per-request cache stats, and the full token decoding trace. Keep these artifacts tied to experiment run ids.
- Use bench-recorder v2 that writes run artifacts to S3 path: s3://redwood-experiments/ml/kv-frag/<run-id>/
- Tag runs with model_commit_hash and runtime_image. Include the config snapshot (json) used for cache parameters.

Quick checklist for running a full sweep
- [ ] pickup baseline run on fp16 single-shard for 8k/32k/128k
- [ ] enable continuous-batching ON and OFF runs
- [ ] run quantized variants (4bit and int8) on same hardware
- [ ] collect token traces and compute token_divergence & mention_recall
- [ ] run attention tracing for a subset (costly) to compute ASI
- [ ] surface failing probes to triage board (label: kv-frag)

Notes and open questions (scratchpad)
- How does the runtime decide shard boundaries in mixed-size prefix inputs? Need a microdesign doc link. Suspect off-by-one in coalesce window.
- Should we add synthetic adversarial prefixes (repeating tokens of pattern P) to trigger attention degeneracy more predictably? Might help surface kernel bugs.
- Consider lightweight in-request checksum for required retrieval spans so the generator can assert that the retrieval piece was applied (binary signal for regression detection).

Appendix: example short programmatic test case (pseudo)
- create doc_P = load_text(\"long_report_22k.txt\")
- send generate(model=fp16, prompt=doc_P) -> store shard_id
- send generate(model=fallback, prompt=\"weather note\") -> cause different shard
- send continue(model=fp16, prompt=\"continue docP:\") -> capture tokens
- compare to baseline continuation; compute scores and stash artifacts
